name: Feathered Crest Induction
description: Converts hair follicles along the scalp's mohawk line into feather-producing follicles, creating a crest of genuine feathers along the crown of the head. The feathers are structurally authentic — barbs, barbules, and rachis — and can be produced in any color combination using chromatophore co-modification. Peacock-iridescent crests are the current fashion peak in GLMZ. The feathers grow, molt, and regrow on a cycle similar to modified hair. They can be styled, trimmed, and arranged like hair but have the unmistakable texture and light-catching properties of real plumage. Lacuna Genomics offers full-head feather conversion for users who want to replace all their hair with plumage, but the mohawk crest remains the most popular configuration. The feathers are waterproof and self-maintaining through preening — a behavior that users develop naturally.
source_organism: Pavo cristatus (Indian peafowl), Goura victoria (Victoria crowned pigeon, structural coloration)
procedure: Scalp retroviral injection converting follicle type, 2 sessions
expression_time: 6–10 weeks for first feather emergence; full crest at 4 months
reversibility: Reversible with follicle reconversion; hair regrows normally
side_effects: Feathers molt — user sheds feathers continuously at low rates
Preening behavior develops unconsciously — users stroke and arrange their crest without realizing it
Feathers are more fragile than hair — damage is visible and takes weeks to regrow
Pillow destruction from feather interaction during sleep
social_perception: Exotic and fashionable. Feather crests are less common than horns or tails but growing in popularity. The peacock-iridescent crest is considered the height of cosmetic geneware art. Some traditional cultures object to humans wearing feathers they didn't earn.
story_hooks: A feather-crested individual's plumage begins producing patterns that match a Lacuna Genomics proprietary genetic watermark — their street-clinic installation used stolen gene sequences
A molted feather found at a restricted location contains the owner's full genetic profile, making feather-crested individuals uniquely traceable
